title: Kanban for One — a calm personal board
description: A polished single-person kanban board (Backlog, Doing, Review, Done) with pointer drag-and-drop that also works on touch, keyboard moves, editable WIP limits that warn visually, colour-coded tags, inline editing and a search filter. The board saves to localStorage and can be exported and imported as JSON.
prompt: Build me a personal kanban board (Backlog / Doing / Review / Done) that I'd actually use. Build drag-and-drop on pointer events so it works on touch, and make every move possible from the keyboard too: focus a card and use [ and ], or arrows with a modifier, with an aria-live announcer saying what happened. Add WIP limits that visually warn, tags with colours, inline editing, a search filter, persistence to localStorage, and JSON export/import. It should feel polished and calm, in one self-contained HTML file.

methodology: Keyboard-first functional tests: every move is made with [, ], Alt+arrows and Enter, and each is checked through the aria-live announcer text and the resulting column order.
Real pointer drag using page.mouse down/move/up on the grip handle, asserting the card's final column and index, then a reload to prove persistence.
WIP boundary tests: a column moves from ok to at to over as cards arrive, the over-limit note appears, and raising the limit clears the warning.
Round-trip data tests: the exported download is parsed and checked, a crafted import replaces the board with unknown tags dropped, and a malformed file is rejected without touching state.
Search/filter checks count only the cards that are actually visible. This caught a real bug where the hidden attribute lost to display:grid.
Responsive review at 1280px (four columns) and 390px (stacked columns).
risks: Drag on touch: scrolling and dragging conflict; the grip uses touch-action:none to separate them.
Focus loss after re-render, which would break keyboard flows and screen-reader context.
Importing hostile or malformed JSON and corrupting saved state.
qa.playwright: Most of the board was straightforward to automate with data-testid and role locators, and the aria-live announcer doubled as an oracle for every move. Drag-and-drop was the tricky part. Playwright's dragTo does not reliably drive a custom pointer-event implementation, so the spec uses page.mouse with stepped moves over the grip. On the Pixel 7 project the columns stack, so the spec first scrolls the source card to a known position so the target is on screen. Export is verified through page.waitForEvent('download') and import through setInputFiles with in-memory buffers, so no fixture files are needed. No screenshots are asserted; the checks cover structure and state.
coverage: Keyboard column moves, reordering, the edge-of-board message and focus retention
Pointer drag between columns, persisted across reload
WIP limit states (at/over), the warning note and an editable limit
Add card, inline edit with tag toggles, and search by text and #tag
JSON export contents, a valid import, and rejection of an invalid import

a11y: Cards are focusable list items labelled with their title, tags, column and position. Every move, edit, WIP warning and import is announced in an assertive live region. All controls are native buttons and labelled inputs with visible focus.
